## Natural history notes

A small noctuid moth characterized by mottled brown, reddish-brown, and tan forewings with angular pale markings and darker patches that help it blend into bark and dead leaves. In Florida, it is found in humid gardens, forests, hammocks, parks, greenhouses, and shaded yards where ferns grow. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on ferns such as Boston fern and brake fern, sometimes becoming noticeable on ornamental ferns in nurseries or landscapes.
